sources.citation: Connell, Bruce. 1997. The integrity of Mambiloid. Paper presented at WOCAL 2, Leipzig, 27 July - 3 August 1997.http://www.mambila.info/Connell/Integ/Integrity.html
sources.note: Zero mentions of Bung or Boung; tone is discussed for other Mambiloid languages only, not Bung.

sources.citation: Embleton, Sheila & Eric S. Wheeler. 2025. On the success and limitations of a quantitative study of geographic and dialect distance. LACUS Forum 50:2, 24-34. Linguistic Association of Canada and the United States (CC BY-NC 3.0).
sources.note: No statement about Bung (or any lect's) stress or tone system; it establishes only that a tone-transcribed digital version of Connell's Mambiloid wordlists, apparently including Bung, exists ('Connell, Bruce. (unpublished) Data for Mambila languages. Glendon College, York University, Toronto') and was reduced to consonant strings for the analysis. Wordlist-level tone MARKS at best, not a statement.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2024. An overview of the Bantoid languages. Afrika und Übersee 97: 1-46. DOI 10.15460/auue.2024.97.1.288.
sources.note: speaker-count table row only; Table 8 'Tone systems in Bantoid and Bantu' (p.23-24) names no target language of this group except Manta ('Western | Manta | H, M, L | SIL Wordlists', already seen for Manta in round 1)

sources.citation: Connell, Bruce, David Zeitlyn, Sascha Griffiths, Laura Hayward & Marieke Martin. 2021. Language ecology, language endangerment, and relict languages: Case studies from Adamawa (Cameroon-Nigeria). Open Linguistics 7(1): 244-300. doi:10.1515/opli-2021-0011 (CC-BY 4.0).
sources.note: No phonology content for Bung: the only Bung material is the status sentence quoted and a map point. The whole paper has one prosodic remark, about Wawa ('tonal contrasts', citing Martin 2012), and cites Connell 2010b 'Somyev Segmental and Tonal Contrasts' (ELAR); nothing on stress, accent or tone for Bung or Kwanja-Ndung.

sources.note: No descriptive reference (0 grammar/phonology/sketch items); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Connell, Bruce. 2007. Endangered languages in Central Africa. In Matthias Brenzinger (ed.), Language Diversity Endangered, 163-178. Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter.
sources.note: Glottolog's second reference for Bung ('dormant'); an overview chapter, so at most a status line, but it is the only other item citing Bung.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 1999. Mambila linguistic field research January 1999: preliminary report.http://www.mambila.info/blench99.html;plus VIMS pages (Connell abstracts, 1996 publication list, Mambila dialect survey project page with Mambiloid bibliography, AHRC borderland project, Mambila bibliography)
sources.note: Zero mentions of Bung/Boung on any of these pages; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Connell, Bruce. 1997. Moribund languages of the Nigeria-Cameroon borderland. Paper presented at the Symposium on Language Endangerment in Africa, Leipzig, 29-31 July 1997 (conference text of Connell 1998, in Brenzinger (ed.) Endangered Languages in Africa, 207-225, Cologne: Koeppe). Hosted at the Virtual Institute of Mambila Studies,http://www.mambila.info/Connell/Mori/Moribundlngs.html
sources.note: Nothing. Section 2.5 'Bung' (about 150 words) is sociolinguistic and lexical only: three rememberers, best one non-native; spoken at Boung on the Adamawa Plateau; the wordlist 'shows its greatest resemblance to be with Ndung-Kwanja' (possibly transfer from the speaker's dominant language), shares items with Tep, Somyev and Vute, plus unidentified items possibly of Adamawa provenance. No phonology, no mention of stress, accent or tone for Bung anywhere in the paper.
Article is a paraphrase of Connell 1998 (3 speakers in 1995, resemblance to Ndung Kwanja); explicitly contains no phonology or stress information.
